name: Adobe Experience Agent USA
description: Adobe Experience Agent USA is a polite, patient AI shopping assistant for main--citisignal--sirugh.aem.live. skills.name: add_to_cart
skills.description:
Create (if needed) a cart and add the specified products.

Cart prices include subtotal_excluding_tax and grand_total, each
with value and currency. Each cart line carries its quantity.
Items Commerce refuses are absent from the cart and reported in
user_errors.

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    items: List of items to add. Each item should have: sku (string), quantity (number), and optionally selected_options (list of strings for configurable/bundle products)
    cart_id: Existing cart ID. If not provided, a new guest cart will be created.
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Required when adding to existing cart, not needed for new guest cart flows and can be empty in this case.

skills.name: categories_data
skills.description:
Get a category and up to three levels of its descendants by ID.

Directly calls the Commerce `categories` GraphQL query with
`subtree: {depth: 3, startLevel: 1}` and returns the matching
category along with descendants up to three levels deep. Use the
default `category_id="1"` (the Commerce root) to walk the whole
catalog; re-invoke with a deeper node to fetch beyond three levels.

Args:
    category_id: Category ID to fetch. Defaults to "1", the catalog root.

skills.name: create_payment_order
skills.description:
Creates a Payment Services (PayPal) order for the cart.

Call this BEFORE set_payment_method for any Payment Services wallet method
(Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal Smart Buttons). The returned `id` (PayPal
order ID) and `mp_order_id` must be passed into set_payment_method's
`payment_method` dict.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants with the Payment Services module.

NOT idempotent: every call creates a new PayPal order. Do not retry after a
timeout or error without first establishing whether an earlier call
succeeded — each retry leaves an extra open order on the PayPal side.

Returns:
- id: PayPal order ID (pass as `paypal_order_id` to set_payment_method)
- mp_order_id: internal Payment Services order ID (pass as `payments_order_id`)
- status: PayPal order status (e.g. "CREATED")
- amount: order amount
- currency_code: e.g. "USD"
On failure, returns {error, message, cart_id} instead of the fields above.
A tenant without the Payment Services module fails this way, with the
underlying GraphQL error in `error`; call get_payment_configuration first to
confirm the tenant has a Payment Services wallet method configured.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    method_code: Payment Services method code, e.g.
        "payment_services_paypal_google_pay",
        "payment_services_paypal_smart_buttons",
        "payment_services_paypal_apple_pay"
    payment_source: Payment source identifier, e.g. "googlepay",
        "paypal", "apple_pay", "hosted_fields"
    location: Storefron...

skills.name: get_available_payment_methods
skills.description:
Retrieves available payment methods for a cart. Requires billing address to be set first.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: get_available_shipping_methods
skills.description:
Retrieves available shipping methods for a cart. Requires shipping address to be set first.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: get_cart
skills.description:
Get current cart contents, totals, and item details by cart ID.

Returns cart data including items (each with uid, sku, name, quantity, price),
and prices (subtotal_excluding_tax and grand_total, each with value and
currency). Use the item uid from this response when calling remove_from_cart.

Also returns the checkout state already set on the cart, so callers can read
it back without repeating the setter calls:
- email: guest email (null until set_guest_email)
- shipping_addresses: [] until set_shipping_address; each entry carries the
  address, available_shipping_methods (the options for that address) and
  selected_shipping_method (null until set_shipping_method)
- billing_address: null until set_billing_address
- selected_payment_method: {code, title}; code is empty until
  set_payment_method

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID (returned by add_to_cart when creating a new cart)
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: get_payment_configuration
skills.description:
Lists the Payment Services methods enabled for a storefront location.

Read-only, no cart needed. Each method carries its Commerce code, who processes
it, which provider environment the merchant is in, and the public identifiers a
wallet integration needs to resolve it (e.g. Google Pay `gateway` /
`gatewayMerchantId` via the processor). Nothing returned is a secret.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants with the Payment Services module installed.
Tenants without the module return an error.
Timeouts, HTTP failures and unexpected GraphQL errors also return an error;
do not substitute a default payment environment on these failures.

Returns:
- location: the normalized location that was queried
- methods: [{code, provider, environment, provider_config}]
  - code: Payment Services method code; match on it to find the method you
    need, e.g. "payment_services_paypal_google_pay" for Google Pay
  - provider: who processes the method; "paypal" today, null if unrecognised
  - environment: "sandbox" | "production" | null. Read from the merchant's
    Payment Services configuration. null means the tenant's Commerce version
    does not expose it (Payment Services < 2.15.0); fall back to your own
    default rather than treating it as an error.
  - provider_config: public identifiers for `provider`. For "paypal":
    client_id, merchant_id and, when set, buyer_country.
- capability (optional): set when the module answered but the method an
  agent is looking for is not enabled for t...

skills.name: get_payment_order
skills.description:
Retrieves the status of a Payment Services (PayPal) order.

Read-only. Call after `create_payment_order` and the wallet token
confirmation step to verify the PayPal order reached `APPROVED`
before calling `place_order`. If status is still `CREATED`, the
payment source has not been confirmed and `place_order` will fail.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants with the Payment Services module.

Returns:
- id: PayPal order ID
- mp_order_id: internal Payment Services order ID
- status: PayPal order status (CREATED, APPROVED, COMPLETED, etc.)
- payment_source_details (optional): card name and last digits when
  the payment source has been attached
On failure, returns {error, message, cart_id} instead of the fields above.
An unknown `paypal_order_id` fails this way (Payment Services returns no
order), as does a tenant without the Payment Services module, with the
underlying GraphQL error in `error`.

Args:
    cart_id: Cart ID the PayPal order is associated with
    paypal_order_id: The PayPal order ID (`id` from create_payment_order)

skills.name: place_order
skills.description:
Places the order for a cart. The cart must have items, a billing address, a payment
method, and for non-virtual carts, shipping information (address and method).
This operation is irreversible.

For Adobe Payment Services wallet methods (Google Pay, Apple Pay, PayPal),
the PayPal order attached via set_payment_method must already be confirmed
with the wallet token before calling this; otherwise Commerce rejects the
placement and the cart is left intact.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Returns:
- number: the placed order number
- token: the order token (guest order lookups)
On failure returns the standard error envelope; `error` carries the
Commerce error code(s) and message(s), e.g.
"Order placement failed: UNDEFINED: Error happened when processing the request."

Args:
    cart_id: Cart ID to place order for
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: product_data
skills.description:
Get full product details from Adobe Catalog Service by SKU.

Returns comprehensive data not available in product_search results: full description,
all images/videos, complete pricing with adjustments, stock status, input customization
options, related product links, and for configurable products, all variant option
definitions with swatches.

Returns JSON with:
- products: array containing the product object with fields:
  - sku, name, description, shortDescription, url, urlKey
  - inStock, lowStock, addToCartAllowed
  - images: [{url, label, roles}], videos: [{url, title}]
  - price (simple products): {final/regular: {amount: {value, currency}}}
  - priceRange (configurable): {minimum/maximum: {final/regular: {amount: {value, currency}}}}
  - options (configurable): [{id, title, required, values: [{id, title, inStock}]}]
  - inputOptions: customization fields (text, file upload, etc.)

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    sku: The exact product SKU (case-sensitive). Must match exactly — use product_search to find it if unknown.
  ...

skills.name: product_facets
skills.description:
List filterable attributes with values and product counts for a scoped context.

Lightweight discovery tool that returns only facets, no product items. Use this to
enumerate what can be filtered and how (eq/in vs range) before calling product_search.
Use returned bucket IDs/values directly as filter values in product_search.

To scope facets to a category, pass filter=[{"attribute": "categories", "eq": "<path>"}]
(use the category's path, e.g. "travel-gifts" or "men/tops-men" — not its numeric id).
With no args, returns facets across the whole catalog. For phrase-based category
discovery, use search_categories instead.

Note: uses tenant configuration from connection context (X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.).

Returns:
- total_count: products matching the context
- facets: [{attribute, title, type, buckets}]
  - ScalarBucket {title, count, id} — use id in eq/in filters
  - RangeBucket {title, count, from, to} — use from/to in range filters
  - CategoryView {title, count, id, path} — category facets with url path
  - StatsBucket {min, max} — numeric range boundaries
- capability (optional): "no_merchandising_facets" when products exist
  but the tenant has published no Live Search facets. When present,
  skip facet-driven discovery and use product_search directly.
- hint (optional): human-readable guidance for the above capability.

Args:
    filter: Optional filter clauses. Each clause has "attribute" plus one operator:
        - "eq": exact match. {"attribute": "ca...

skills.name: product_recommendations
skills.description:
Get product recommendations from Adobe Commerce for a given product SKU.

Returns AI-powered recommendation units with recommended products, including pricing
information. Recommendation types include "Customers who viewed this also viewed",
"Customers who bought this also bought", "Recommended for you", and more.

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    current_sku: The SKU of the product to get recommendations for (e.g., 'ADB229')
    page_type: The page context for recommendations (default: "Product").
               Valid values: Product, Category, Cart, Checkout, CMS, PageBuilder.

skills.name: product_search
skills.description:
Search products via Adobe Live Search.

Prefer filter over phrase for structured queries — phrase uses fuzzy matching and skews
facet counts. Discovery flow: call search_categories(phrase) first when the user's
intent may span multiple categories, then product_facets(filter=[{"attribute": "categories", "eq": "<path>"}])
per selected category to see filterable attributes and values. Use searchable_attributes
only as a fallback when an attribute code hasn't appeared in a recent facets response.
Use products_data with a list of result SKUs for full product details.

Note: uses tenant configuration from connection context (X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.).

Returns a structured object (delivered as MCP structuredContent) with:
- total_count, page_info {current_page, page_size, total_pages}
- items: [{productView: {sku, name, price/priceRange, images, inStock, url, description, shortDescription, attributes}, highlights, applied_query_rule}]
- suggestions, related_terms
On failure, returns {error, message, phrase} instead of the fields above.

Args:
    phrase: Optional search keywords (e.g., 'running shoes'). Omit or pass None for filter-only searches — this avoids fuzzy matching interference with facet counts.
    current_page: Page number starting at 1 (default: 1)
    page_size: Results per page (default: 20)
    filter: List of filter clauses. Each clause has "attribute" and exactly one operator:
        - "eq": exact string match. Example: {"attribute": "brand", "eq...

skills.name: product_variants
skills.description:
Get all available variants for a configurable/complex product by SKU.

Returns variant selections (option combinations) along with comprehensive simple product
information including pricing, images, videos, attributes, stock status. Each variant
is a simple product with specific pricing and attributes. Supports filtering by option IDs
and pagination. Useful for displaying all possible product configurations with complete
product details.

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    sku: The exact product SKU of the configurable/complex product to get variants for. You have to use the exact SKU of the product, so call product_search to get it if needed.
    option_ids: Optional array of option IDs to filter variants by specific option combinations
    page_size: Optional number of variants to return per page for pagination
    cursor: Optional pagination cursor for retrieving the next page of variants

skills.name: remove_from_cart
skills.description:
Remove a specific item from a cart by its UID (all quantities will be removed).

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    cart_item_uid: UID of the cart item to remove, get it from the get_cart tool
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: search_categories
skills.description:
Find candidate categories matching a search phrase.

Use as the first step in a discovery flow to resolve which categories are
relevant to the user's query before drilling into filterable attributes.
Follow up with product_facets(filter=[{"attribute":"categories","eq":"<path>"}])
per selected category to explore attributes within that scope. Use the category's
path from this response (not its numeric id) as the filter value.

Returns the full facets response (same shape as product_facets); relevant
categories are in the facet where attribute == "categories" — buckets are
CategoryView type with {id, path, count, title}. May include a
"capability": "no_merchandising_facets" marker when products match but
no facets are published; in that case, fall back to phrase-based search.

Note: uses tenant configuration from connection context (X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.).

Args:
    phrase: Search keywords.

skills.name: searchable_attributes
skills.description:
List attribute codes usable in product_search filter/sort (without values).

The product_facets tool returns the same codes plus their actual values and counts.
Use this tool only as a fallback to validate an attribute code that has not appeared in
a recent product_facets response.

Returns:
- attributes: [{attribute, label, numeric}]
  - attribute: code for filter/sort (e.g. "color", "price", "categories")
  - label: human-readable display name
  - numeric: true → range filter (from/to); false → eq/in filter
- capability (optional): "no_filterable_attributes" when the tenant has
  no attributes marked filterable in Live Search. When present, skip
  facet/attribute discovery and rely on phrase-based product_search.
- hint (optional): human-readable guidance for the above capability.

skills.name: set_billing_address
skills.description:
Sets billing address on cart. Required to get available payment methods and place order.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    address: Billing address object with fields: firstname, lastname, street (array of strings), city, region (string), postcode, country_code (2-letter code e.g. 'US'), telephone. Optional: company, middlename, prefix, suffix, fax, region_id, save_in_address_book. Not required when same_as_shipping is true.
    same_as_shipping: If true, use the shipping address as the billing address. When set, address can be omitted.
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: set_guest_email
skills.description:
Sets email address on a guest cart. Required before checkout can proceed.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    email: Guest email address
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: set_payment_method
skills.description:
Sets the selected payment method on cart.

For generic methods: `{"code": "checkmo"}`.

For Payment Services wallet methods (Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.), first
call `create_payment_order` to obtain `id` and `mp_order_id`, then pass:
```
{
    "code": "payment_services_paypal_google_pay",
    "payment_services_paypal_google_pay": {
        "payments_order_id": "<mp_order_id from create_payment_order>",
        "paypal_order_id": "<id from create_payment_order>",
        "payment_source": "googlepay"
    }
}
```

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    payment_method: Payment method input dict (see above for generic
        and Payment Services shapes)
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: set_shipping_address
skills.description:
Sets shipping address on cart. Required to get available shipping methods.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    address: Shipping address object with fields: firstname, lastname, street (array of strings), city, region (string), postcode, country_code (2-letter code e.g. 'US'), telephone. Optional: company, region_id, save_in_address_book.
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: set_shipping_method
skills.description:
Sets the selected shipping method on cart.

Only available for ACCS/PaaS tenants.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    carrier_code: Shipping carrier code (e.g. 'flatrate', 'freeshipping')
    method_code: Shipping method code (e.g. 'flatrate')
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.

skills.name: update_cart_items
skills.description:
Update quantities of items already in a cart.

Use this tool to change the quantity of one or more items in a cart.
Setting quantity to 0 removes the item from the cart.
Cart prices include subtotal_excluding_tax and grand_total, each
with value and currency.

Note: This tool uses tenant configuration from the connection context (HTTP headers).
Ensure your client provides X-Environment-Id, X-Website-Code, etc.

Args:
    cart_id: Existing cart ID
    cart_items: List of items to update. Each item must have:
        - cart_item_uid (string): UID of the cart item (get it from get_cart)
        - quantity (number): New quantity; set to 0 to remove the item
    auth_token: Authorization token for cart access. Can be empty for guest cart flows.
